newsitem.title: UK: Bradford wooltops follow Australian merinos higher.
newsitem.headline: Bradford wooltops follow Australian merinos higher.

text.p: Tops prices for 58-70s qualities leapt by up to seventeen pence per kg after sterling softened and the superfine indicator at Australia's raw wool auction gained 37 cents, market sources said.
Traders said a positive view of official auctioneer Wool International's progress towards meeting Australia's minimum stockpile disposal targets offered tops values some underlying support.
"Wool International's pricing is closely watched in the trade and the firmer tendency is already being talked about," one market commentator said.
Finest 66 and 70s Supers lead the upward swing, gaining seventeen pence per kg while 64s Blended gambolled to 403 pence per kg, up eight pence.
Topmakers said retailer resistance to higher prices for homegrown wool was keeping a cap on English styles, all of which were quoted unchanged.
Despite the weaker pound exporters said there was little chance of fresh business in the immediate term.
